# 1 Chronicles Chapter 29 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 385r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_029_page_001.jpg

---

**1** King David addressed the entire assembly: "My son Solomon, the one God has chosen, is still young and inexperienced. The task ahead is enormous, for this palace is not for a human being — it is for the LORD God himself.

**2** "With everything I have, I've made preparations for God's house: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, wood for the wood — along with onyx, turquoise, stones of every color, all kinds of precious gems, and fine marble, in vast quantities.

**3** "And beyond all that, because of my personal devotion to God's house, I am giving from my own private treasury of gold and silver — above and beyond what I've already gathered for the holy house: **4** three thousand talents of Ophir gold and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to plate the walls of the buildings. **5** Gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, and resources for the craftsmen. Now — who is willing to consecrate themselves to the LORD today?"

**6** The response was immediate. The family heads, the tribal leaders, the military commanders, and the royal administrators all came forward with their gifts. **7** They gave for the service of God's house: five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron. **8** Anyone who had precious stones contributed them to the temple treasury, under the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.

**9** The people were overjoyed at this outpouring of generosity, because everyone gave to the LORD wholeheartedly. King David too was filled with great joy.

**10** David praised the LORD before the entire assembly. He said:

"Praise be to you, LORD,
God of our father Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.

**11** "Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the power
and the glory and the victory and the majesty.
Everything in heaven and on earth belongs to you.
Yours, LORD, is the kingdom;
you are exalted as ruler over all.

**12** "Wealth and honor come from you alone;
you are the ruler of all things.
In your hands are strength and power,
and it is in your hands to make anyone great and strong.

**13** "So now, our God, we give you thanks
and praise your glorious name.

**14** "But who am I, and who are my people,
that we could give anything at all?
Everything comes from you,
and we have only given back what is already yours.

**15** "We are foreigners and strangers in your sight,
as were all our ancestors.
Our days on earth are like a shadow —
here and then gone, with nothing certain.

**16** "LORD our God, even this wealth we've gathered to build a house for your holy name — it all came from your hand, and it all belongs to you.

**17** "I know, my God, that you examine the heart and are pleased by integrity. I have given all this willingly, from an honest heart. And now I've watched with joy as your people here have given to you willingly as well.

**18** "LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors — keep this desire alive forever in the hearts of your people, and keep their hearts loyal to you. **19** And give my son Solomon a wholehearted desire to obey your commands, your laws, and your decrees, to carry out everything needed, and to build the temple I've planned."

**20** Then David told the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God!" So the entire assembly praised the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and they bowed low and worshiped the LORD and honored the king.

**21** The next day they offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings and abundant additional sacrifices for all Israel.

**22** They ate and drank before the LORD that day with tremendous joy. Then they crowned Solomon son of David as king for the second time, anointing him before the LORD as their ruler, and Zadok as priest.

**23** Solomon took his seat on the LORD's throne as king, succeeding his father David. He thrived, and all Israel gave him their loyalty. **24** Every official, every warrior, and even all of David's other sons pledged themselves to King Solomon.

**25** The LORD elevated Solomon to extraordinary greatness in the eyes of all Israel and gave him a royal splendor that no previous king of Israel had known.

**26** David son of Jesse had reigned over all Israel. **27** He ruled Israel for forty years — seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.

**28** He died at a ripe old age, satisfied with a long life, wealth, and honor. His son Solomon succeeded him as king.

**29** As for the full account of King David's reign, from beginning to end, it is recorded in the writings of Samuel the seer, the writings of Nathan the prophet, and the writings of Gad the seer — **30** including the full story of his reign and his achievements, and the events that affected him, Israel, and all the surrounding kingdoms.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — "not for a human being — it is for the LORD God":** This single sentence explains why the project is so extravagant. The temple's scale matches its intended occupant. David is not building for his dynasty's prestige — he is building a house worthy of the one who made the universe. The *birah* (palace-fortress) is God's address on earth.

**Verse 11 — The great doxology:** This may be the most important prayer in 1 Chronicles. Five attributes are ascribed to God — greatness, power, glory, victory, majesty — and then the sweeping claim: "Everything in heaven and on earth belongs to you." The echo of this prayer in the closing doxology of the Lord's Prayer (Matt 6:13) is not accidental; early Christians recognized David's words as the fitting conclusion to Jesus' prayer.

**Verse 14 — "we have only given back what is already yours":** The deepest truth about human generosity. We own nothing. Every gift we give to God was first given by God to us. David, having just donated a staggering fortune, says in effect: "I gave you nothing — I just returned what was never mine." This is the theology that makes worship possible: not our achievement but our acknowledgment.

**Verse 15 — "foreigners and strangers":** David, at the height of his power, calls himself and all Israel *gerim* — aliens, temporary residents. The king who rules from Jerusalem admits that the earth is not his home. Life is a shadow. This is not despair — it is clarity. Only God endures.

**Verse 28 — "satisfied":** David's death notice is serene. He dies *save'a* — "full," "satisfied" — a word used of someone who has eaten and is content. No mention of Bathsheba, no mention of Absalom, no mention of the plague. The Chronicler gives David the death he deserved at his best.

*— PNEUMA*
